System Map

Read together, the four themes are not separate pressures. Five loops connect them. Debt needs quick returns (R1): borrowed money pushes agents into wider use. Incidents bring in gates (B1): agent incidents prompt government gates that slow new releases. The grid sets the pace (B2): data centre spending runs into grid queues. Fewer juniors learn the job (R2): agents take junior tasks and the pool of experienced staff thins. Incidents force controls (B3): incidents push organisations to build controls into agents. Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single theme carries.

Hover over a status for its meaning: Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now; Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks how strongly loops B1 (incidents bring in gates) and B3 (incidents force controls) work, that is whether the risk of agents falls on the deployers or on those affected; its vertical axis asks how far loop R1 (debt needs quick returns) runs, that is whether the build-out is paid for with borrowed money or from earnings.

What it means: the loop that links the four themes is R1 (debt needs quick returns): the same borrowed money that builds the data centres pushes agents into use faster than controls are built, which feeds the incidents that bring in gates and the junior tasks agents absorb. The levers an organisation controls are what its agents can reach, the evidence it keeps for regulators, how it funds AI and whether it keeps hiring juniors.
